newsitem.title: USA: Clinton's lead narrows to 11 points in California.
newsitem.headline: Clinton's lead narrows to 11 points in California.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lead in California over Republican rival Bob Dole has narrowed to 11 points, according to a poll published on Monday.
The poll by the independent Field Institute showed Clinton leading Dole 47 percent to 36 percent in California, the most populous state and biggest electoral prize.
A Field poll published in late October showed Clinton leading Dole 52 percent to 34 percent in the state.

The new Field poll, carried out Oct. 29 to Nov. 3, also showed that Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot was preferred by 7 percent of likely voters while Ralph Nader of the Green Party had the support of 5 percent. Three percent of those surveyed were undecided.

When supporters for Perot, Nader and other candidates were asked who they would vote for if the race were limited to just Clinton and Dole, their preferences divided 52 percent to 18 percent in Clinton's favour, the poll said.

The Field poll also found that the Democratic lead over Republicans across California's 52 congressional races was just three percentage points in the closing days of the campaign, down from 10 points in late October.

The new Field poll was based on a representative statewide sample of 998 likely voters in Tuesday's presidential election. The margin of error from the overall sample was plus or minus 3.2 percentage points, the Field Institute said.
